title: AgentBehaviorBench: A Benchmark of Real-World Behavioural Failures in AI Agents
summary: AgentBehaviorBench studies real-world behavioural failures reported by users of AI agents. The benchmark contains 43 validated issues from 23 open-source agents, linking issue reports to specific source revisions, reproducing test cases, execution trajectories, and root-cause and fault-location annotations.

The paper evaluates coding agents on behavioural failure detection and fault localization. In the detection task, testing agents generate cases from high-level task descriptions without access to the original issue report. In the localization task, they receive the full issue report and can inspect the target codebase and execution environment.
finding: Within 50 test executions per issue, Codex and Claude Code trigger the reported failure in 30.23% and 16.28% of issues, respectively. In the separate fault-localization experiment, both correctly explain the root cause of 41 out of 43 issues. The results highlight a gap between diagnosing a reported failure and generating tests that expose it.
